Westwater Resources ( (WWR) ) has provided an announcement.

On September 14, 2026, Westwater Resources’ Executive Chairman Terence Cryan presented the company’s updated business plan at the H.C. Wainwright 28th Annual Global Investment Conference, coinciding with the posting of an investor presentation on its website. The materials highlighted Westwater’s progress on its Kellyton Graphite Plant, where more than half of the planned $245 million capital cost has been invested and an EXIM loan approved, as well as its broader mine-to-market graphite strategy centered on U.S. battery demand.

The update underscored that Phase 1 of the Kellyton facility is designed to provide 12,500 mtpa of battery-grade natural graphite, with Phase 2 expected to lift capacity to 50,000 mtpa, supported by ongoing customer qualification and offtake discussions. By advancing a strategically located, vertically integrated graphite operation at a time when the U.S. imports all battery-grade natural graphite and relies heavily on Chinese supply, the company is seeking to strengthen its industry positioning and appeal to stakeholders focused on domestic, secure battery-materials sourcing.

More about Westwater Resources

Westwater Resources, Inc. is a U.S.-based developer of battery-grade natural graphite, positioning itself as a mine-to-market supplier to the electric vehicle and energy storage sectors. The company’s Coosa Graphite Deposit in Coosa County, Alabama, and its Kellyton Graphite Plant in Kellyton, Alabama, place it in the heart of the U.S. Battery Corridor near major EV and battery manufacturing hubs.

Westwater aims to become the first U.S. producer of battery-grade natural graphite through vertically integrated operations that connect domestic resource development with processing, targeting coated spherical purified graphite for lithium-ion battery anodes. Its strategy focuses on phased plant development, leveraging experienced leadership and growing demand for non-Chinese, domestically sourced graphite amid policy support for a secure U.S. battery supply chain.

data.title: TransDigm Prices Larger 2035 Senior Secured Notes Offering
data.description:
TransDigm Group Incorporated Shs Unsponsored Brazilian Depositary Receipt Repr 0.02 Sh ( (BR:T1DG34) ) has provided an announcement.

On September 14, 2026, TransDigm Group announced that its subsidiary TransDigm Inc. had priced a $3,000 million offering of 6.75% Senior Secured Notes due 2035, increased from an initially planned $2,500 million. The notes, issued at par and guaranteed by TransDigm Group and select subsidiaries, are being privately placed under Rule 144A and Regulation S, with closing expected on September 28, 2026, subject to customary conditions.

TransDigm Group plans to use the net proceeds to repurchase all of TransDigm Inc.’s outstanding 6.75% Senior Secured Notes due 2028 through a concurrent tender offer launched on September 14, 2026, and for general corporate purposes. The transaction effectively extends the company’s debt maturity profile and may support its ongoing financial flexibility, although the notes will remain restricted to qualified institutional buyers and certain non U.S. investors under securities law exemptions.

data.title: TransAlta Ordered to Keep Centralia Unit 2 Available for 90 More Days
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from TransAlta ( (TSE:TA) ).

On September 14, 2026, TransAlta said its U.S. subsidiary TransAlta Centralia Generation LLC received an order from the Department of Energy covering its Centralia Unit 2 in Washington state. The order mandates the coal-fired unit remain available for operation for 90 days, until December 12, 2026, extending its availability beyond previously anticipated timelines.

Once the order takes effect, TransAlta intends to comply and coordinate with the Department of Energy and Washington state authorities regarding the unit’s status. The move underscores the continuing role of legacy thermal generation in grid reliability, with potential implications for regional power supply and TransAlta’s short-term operational planning at Centralia.

data.title: Yarrow Bioscience Announces Underwritten Equity Offering Agreement
data.description:
Yarrow Bioscience ( (YARW) ) just unveiled an update.

On September 10, 2026, Yarrow Bioscience entered an underwriting agreement with Jefferies, TD Securities and Guggenheim Securities to sell 5,769,231 shares of common stock at $26.00 per share, using its effective shelf registration. The underwriters exercised in full a 30-day option on September 11, 2026 to purchase an additional 865,384 shares, bringing expected net proceeds to about $161.8 million, with the offering slated to close on September 14, 2026.

The capital raise strengthens Yarrow Bioscience’s balance sheet and provides funding flexibility, while directors and executives agreed to 60-day lock-up arrangements that limit insider share sales and support market stability for the new issuance. The company also provided customary indemnification to underwriters against certain liabilities, reflecting standard capital-markets practice and underscoring the formal structure of the transaction.

data.title: Niki BioSolutions Highlights Strategic Synergies in Alzheimer’s Diagnostics
data.description:
Niki BioSolutions Inc ( (NIKI) ) just unveiled an announcement.

Niki BioSolutions Inc operates in the biotechnology and molecular diagnostics sector, focusing on non-invasive, blood-based tests for Alzheimer’s disease and broader brain health, alongside rare disease and neuro-oncology applications. Through its DiamiR Biosciences subsidiary, the company runs a CLIA-licensed, CAP-accredited, New York State–licensed lab in New Haven, Conn., built around proprietary microRNA, protein biomarker, and genotyping platforms aimed at a large unmet need in neurodegenerative disease diagnostics.

The company, formed via an all-stock merger completed on July 20, 2026 between Aptorum Group Limited and DiamiR Biosciences Corp., used a September 2026 investor conference presentation to outline strategic synergies in diagnostics and therapeutics, dual growth engines in pharma and clinical services, and a pipeline spanning Alzheimer’s risk tests to oncology and infectious disease programs. The materials emphasize revenue-generating pharma services, early-stage clinical diagnostics, and a broadened leadership and IP base, underscoring Niki BioSolutions’ bid to strengthen its position in the evolving Alzheimer’s testing market and support drug development in an area long plagued by trial failures.
